reason: A peristome or costa type named after Fissidens bryoides. It refers to a reference species, so it means nothing without that species. It is not a quality in its own right.
The wings (wing petal PO_0025325) are as long as the standard (banner petal PO_0025324). This is equality with another part, not a term.

label: acaulescent
definition: A shape quality inhering in a whole plant by virtue of its stem being so short that the leaves and inflorescences appear to arise directly from the ground.
reason: French acaule means stemless. The plant still has a stem, only a very short one, so 'stem absent' would be false. No PATO or FLOPO term covers it.
A compound of two existing values, lanceolate (PATO_0001877) and filiform (PATO_0104351), annotated as a continuum like linear-lanceolate.

target: new: two values of one bearer (conjunction)
reason: The apex tapers (attenuate PATO_0001982) to a blunt tip (obtuse PATO_0001935). Both values hold at once, so this is not a continuum and not a new shape.
A compound of sericeous (PATO_0104358) and villous (FLOPO:0991051). It is an intermediate covering of hairs between two existing values.
A grass's growing season, usually standing for C3 photosynthesis. It is a trait of plant physiology or agronomy, not a quality of form, and its boundaries are vague.
Crinite means bearing long, weak hairs in tufts or a mane. That is the long hairs confined to a tuft or zone of 'bearded'.
Same reading as the earlier rule for 'powdery' (C343 mealy). 'White' is the colour of the powder, not of the stem. 'Not white powdery' is the negation.

The statements come from lichens (for example Leptotrema), where muriform means ascospores divided by cross and lengthwise walls. These are fungal spores, not plant spores, so the bearer mapping is wrong.
French 'en relief' veins stand out from the leaf surface: PATO prominent, standing out or projecting beyond a surface.
A compound of puberulous (FLOPO:0991049) and tomentose (PATO_0002341), annotated as a continuum between two existing values.
A bunch grass grows in dense tufts or clumps from the base. That is caespitose.
A vine-like habit means stems that climb or lean on other plants. 'Somewhat vine-like' takes the approximate-value pattern.

label: cymosely branched
definition: A branched quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of each of the bearer's axes ending in a flower or bud, with further growth continuing from lateral branches arising below it, as in a cyme.
reason: PO has cyme inflorescence (PO_0030126) as a part, but no quality for cyme-type branching. It is a sibling of the inflorescence-architecture values (raceme-like, thyrse-like), and it also applies to stems.
A partial tint of an unstated colour. The part as a whole is not dark, so low brightness would be wrong, and the colour and where it lies are missing.
'Leaf phyllodial' says the leaf is a phyllode, which is a part in PO (synonyms phyllode, phyllodium).
It negates 'scapose', which has no term yet. A scape maps to peduncle, so 'scape absent' would wrongly read as 'peduncle absent'. Decide on scapose first.
Wire-like means slender and thread-like, the same reading as the earlier rules for thread-like and hair-like. Stiffness, if stated, is the separate value inflexible.
Ribbon-like means long, narrow and flat, like ligulate (rule C189). PATO band shaped is a strip that encircles something, so it does not fit.
Rough because of minute teeth on angles, margins and apices. The roughness is scabrous, and there is no separate term for denticulate.
A relation stated without its second term, as for 'contiguous'. PATO_0002259 adjacent to is relational.

target: new: division of the segments (leaf pinnate; pinnae bipinnatifid)
reason: The leaf is pinnate (PATO_0000410) and its pinnae are twice pinnatifid. That is two values on the leaf and its parts, not one new value.
Moss exostome teeth finely marked with lines across their long axis. 'Not cross striolate' is the negation.
A stegocarpous moss capsule opens by a lid (operculum). Unlike cleistocarpous capsules, it has one, so presence of the part states it.
French 'non anastomosées' veins = not anastomosing.

label: callus-tipped
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's apex ending in a small, hard, thickened point or knob (a callosity).
reason: A sibling of spine-tipped (FLOPO:0991210). It sits under shape rather than pointed, because callous tips can be rounded ('broad rounded callous-tipped teeth'). 'Callus' alone is a generic part that was rejected.

label: hypostomatous
definition: A spatial pattern quality inhering in a leaf by virtue of its stomata being confined to its abaxial surface.
reason: Stomata on the lower surface only. One presence rule (stomatal complex PO_0002000) cannot say 'only', so a value class is needed. Amphistomatous would be its sibling.
Deltate = triangular (rule C226), so lance-deltate = PATO lanceolate-triangular.
The absence of a generic 'membrane' ('membrane' was rejected as a generic part). What the membrane is differs between seed and hypanthium, so no one part can be named absent.
